0563f1f586f39625.question: What does the customer want, and has the bank promised anything so far?

answer.answer: The customer wants to know the real reason their Everyday credit card application was declined. They also say the decline was not fair and suspect it was due to their postcode. The file records no promise, commitment or offer made by the bank so far. Note 1 only records that the application was declined by an automated scorecard on 24/10 and that the decline letter did not name the credit reference agency. Under LND-2, declined customers must be told the main reason where possible and which credit reference agency was used. Complaints handlers must not overturn a lending decision; complaints about declines are reviewed by Lending Specialists.

answer.answer: 24/10: the Everyday credit card application was declined by an automated scorecard. The customer says it was declined "in seconds with no reason". cc27bfa219193101.question: Which policy rules decide this case, and what do they require the handler to do?

answer.answer: This is a complaint about a declined credit card application. LND-2 requires declined customers to be told the main reason where possible and the credit reference agency used; note_1 records the decline letter did not state the agency. LND-2 also says a decline complaint is reviewed by Lending Specialists and the handler must not overturn the decision. ESC-1 routes lending decisions to Lending Specialists, within 2 business days (ESC-2), with all ten ESC-3 fields. The handler stays the customer's contact until the specialist accepts the handover (ESC-5). The outcome and any redress are decided by an authorised person (CH-8). The file does not show the actual decline reason or whether postcode was a factor.
